title: Done Means Done
tagline: The AI doesn't get to say it's done. The proof does.
what: My plan board shows what's finished, what still needs checking and what needs my yes. Goals close on a command's output, a separate AI's sign-off or my own words, not the working chat's say-so.
built: Every stage of a plan gets 2 to 5 goals before work starts, each naming the proof that will close it
Goals tick themselves off when that proof shows up in the chat's record, not on the AI's say-so
A sign-off only counts from a separate AI. The working chat typing one counts for nothing.
My yes has to be my own words, typed by me in that chat. Made-up quotes get refused.
credit: Built it on top of Claude Code
starring: Me, and the AI chats I run every day

making.problem: Halfway through a big job I couldn't tell how far along it really was, what was left, or when the work had wandered off.

steps.name: Define done
steps.says: When I approve a plan, I'm approving the goals that say when each stage is finished.

steps.name: Watch for proof
steps.says: At the end of every turn, the chat's record is scanned for that proof.

steps.name: Close on proof
steps.says: A goal closes only on the evidence. Dropping one takes a written reason I can see.

moment.what: I can look at the plan and see which goals have proof, which are still open and which are waiting for me. Each closed goal carries the evidence that closed it.

rows: It builds on a clean copy
